st: Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Set it aside.
Lower the heat to medium and cook the onions and garlic for [[5 minutes]] until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes until thick and jammy.
Return the chicken to the pot with [[3 cups]] water, the whole chili and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of hot broth until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens, the oil rises and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Meanwhile rinse the rice and cook it with [[4 cups]] water and a pinch of salt, covered on low, for 15 minutes.
Remove the chili. Serve the chicken and sauce over the rice.
Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper in a large bowl. Add the onions and chicken and toss to coat.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least [[2 hours]].
Lift the chicken out of the marinade and pat dry. Keep the onions and liquid.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side, then set aside.
Add the onions with their marinade and the chili. Cook on medium for 15 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.
Return the chicken, add [[0.5 cup]] water and the remaining salt. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Taste and add more lemon or salt if needed. Serve with plain rice or bread.
Season the beef with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Heat [[0.33 cup]] oil in a large heavy pot and brown the beef well on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Add the onions and garlic and cook for [[5 minutes]] until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes until thick and the oil separates.
Pour in [[6 cups]] water, add the chili and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the carrots and cabbage. Simmer 10 minutes, then lift the vegetables and beef onto a plate.
Measure the broth; you want about [[4.5 cups]], so add water or boil it down. Season with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Add the rinsed rice, stir once, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes.
Top the rice with the beef and vegetables, cover and steam 5 more minutes. Remove the chili and serve.

ing: frozen cassava leaves, or fresh spinach
smoked fish or fresh white fish
st: Put the beef, one onion, garlic and [[4 cups]] water in a large pot with a pinch of salt. Boil, then cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Thaw the greens if frozen. Chop them finely or pulse them in a blender with a splash of water.
Add the greens and the whole chili to the pot. Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Heat the palm oil in a small pan and cook the remaining onion for 5 minutes until soft. Stir it into the pot.
Add the fish in chunks and simmer for 20 minutes until the greens are very soft and the oil floats on top.
Season with salt, remove the chili, and serve with rice.
Heat the palm oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions and garlic for [[6 minutes]] until soft.
Add [[3 cups]] water, the eggplant, the whole chili and a pinch of salt. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the fish chunks and simmer 8 minutes until just cooked.
Stir in the okra. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and silky.
Meanwhile rinse the rice and cook it with [[4 cups]] water and salt, covered on low, for 15 minutes.
Season the sauce with salt, remove the chili, and serve over the rice.
Put the fonio in a bowl, cover with cold water, swirl and pour off the water. Repeat 2 times to wash away grit.
Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium heat and cook the onion for [[4 minutes]] until soft.
Add [[2.25 cups]] water and [[0.75 tsp]] salt and bring to a boil.
Stir in the drained fonio, cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes to steam.
Fluff with a fork to separate the grains and serve with stew or sauce.
Rinse the hibiscus flowers in cold water.
Bring [[8 cups]] water to a boil. Add the hibiscus and ginger, then turn off the heat.
Cover and steep for [[20 minutes]].
Strain into a pitcher and discard the flowers.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] sugar until dissolved. Add the mint and vanilla if using.
Chill for at least 2 hours and serve over ice.
